newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin backs Lebed for stopping Chechen war.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin backs Lebed for stopping Chechen war.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin gave his security chief Alexander Lebed a vote of confidence on Thursday, saying in a radio address that he had carried out presidential orders in stopping the war in Chechnya.

"My aide Alexander Lebed fulfilled my instruction and stopped the military conflict," Yeltsin said. He also had praise for the Kremlin administration, headed by chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais, and the government of Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, with whom Lebed seems at times to be in conflict.

Lebed signed a peace deal with Chechnya's separatist rebels on August 31 but had a cool reception in Moscow, from the authorities and opposition alike, for apparently leaving open the possibility of Chechen secession in five years time.

The former general was jeered as a "traitor" in the State Duma lower chamber of parliament on Wednesday and clashed with Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov. He left the chamber in frustration after trying to defend his peace plan.

Yeltsin, in a speech broadcast as Chechen separatist leader Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev was due in Moscow, said Russian prisoners must be returned. He warned that the troop withdrawal agreed by Lebed must not lead to Chechens "plundering" their weapons as happened when Soviet forces left Chechnya five years ago.

Yeltsin said Lebed's priority now must be the restoration of a system of government for Chechnya and the reconstruction of its economy. The president repeated the government line that the status and make-up of new ruling bodies should be determined before settling the issue of financial aid.
